results.fact: Ice grade of the route (header grade pill)
results.evidence: Still unsettled on retry. The route database page lists the North Face as 'AI2 Steep Snow', Grade III, matching ice_grade AI2; the row's grade, pitch_detail grade and partner experienceLevel say AI2-3 (the pitch entry frames AI2-3 as the harder-conditions case). No second independent source assigns any AI number: a local outdoors-club report and a personal trip log give only snow angles to 55 degrees. One source is not enough to rewrite three fields.

length_m 21 (~69 ft) still disagrees with beta and pitch_detail, which put the summit scramble at 20-30 ft. One new source agrees with the row's prose (about 20 ft of rock before the ladder, roughly 30 ft of hands-on scrambling in all); two other lookout pages mention only a 'short' scramble and ladder with no figure. With one external figure and no source stating a 'climb length' for this hike, no replacement value (and no conversion of a range) is safe; clearing length_m is a catalog decision rather than a researched fix.

Still unsettled. The row describes the Hester Lake line everywhere (approach, itinerary narrative, waypoints to 7.8 mi one way) but the itinerary/totalNote/partner fields say about 10 mi round trip, the figure for the other (Goat Creek / Price Lake) line. A new source gives Hester Lake alone as 10.8 mi round trip, so 10 mi cannot be right for the Hester line, but published figures for the full Hester Lake route still disagree (13 mi vs 15.6 mi round trip; the row's approach says ~15), so there is no agreed value to write.

results.fact: Whether a parking pass/fee is required at the trailhead
results.evidence: Still conflicting. The trail-association Hester Lake hike page lists a Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass (a club route page reportedly says the same), while the Forest Service Dingford Creek Trailhead page says no pass is currently required. Land-manager and secondary sources disagree, so no two agreeing independent sources settle it.

results.fact: Distance to the Big Beaver Trail junction waypoint
results.evidence: Sources agree the Big Beaver Creek crossing / Big Beaver camp area is about 6.5-7 mi from the Ross Dam trailhead (Pierce Creek at 6 mi, bridge about a mile further), matching the approach prose and the 12 mi at Thirtynine Mile Camp. But the waypoint's stored pin sits about a mile from the trailhead near Ross Dam, where the Big Beaver Trail begins; setting distMi to 7 would make the list disagree with the map pin, and renaming it to the dam-end start is a pin/identity decision out of scope. Left open.

results.fact: Climbing season window (Jul-Sep chip vs a stated Jul-Oct/May-Oct window elsewhere)
results.evidence: Retry found only generic Snow Lake / Gem Lake hiking guidance (mid-July through October, trails snow-free after early July), not a month window for the Roosevelt gully itself; sources specific to the scramble say only that the gully must be dry and snow-free. The itinerary.cal 'May through October' remains the weakest claim but no two independent sources state the scramble's window, so no patch.

results.fact: which side of the mountain the route climbs
results.evidence: already consistent. The live row is now named 'East Slopes (via Airplane Lake)' with aspect E and face 'East slopes and east ridge above Airplane Lake', and no field still mentions a southeast line.

Still unsettled. New sources give about 5.5 mi from the border obelisk (a couple of miles past parking) to Ouzel Lake and about 4 mi of flat going before Depot Creek Falls; earlier sources gave ~5 mi washout-to-lake. The start point (road washout vs a spur-road parking) moves between reports, and no two sources give the same current one-way or round-trip figure to replace dist_km 13.7, the 10.3 mi summit waypoint or the ~20-21.5 mi itinerary.

results.fact: road-walk and One Acre Lake distances from the current gate
results.evidence: New sources give 13 mi round trip / 3,500 ft and 13.5 mi round trip from 1,680 ft, and one climbing site gives 6 mi with the old 'impassable within a half mile' start. No source gives distances from the current gate to the second switchback or to One Acre Lake that would settle the waypoints (lake at 3.7 mi) against the approach prose (~6 mi to the lake) and the camp note (5-6 mi road walk).
